title: Assessment of Radioactivity Concentrations and Associated Radiological Health Risk in Natural Spring Mineral Bottled Drinking Water from South Africa
content: Naturally occurring radionuclides are ubiquitous at various levels of concentration while exposure to ionizing radiation by humans is of global concern. The assessment of radiological health risk associated with the consumption of natural spring mineral water is critical for ensuring public health and safety. The study aims at investigating the activity concentration levels of natural radionuclides 226Ra, 232Th and 40K and the associated radiological health risk in commercial natural spring bottled water in South Africa. 21 most consumed brands of bottled water collected from the market were analysed using HPGe gamma detector. The results indicate that activity concentrations ranged from 1.060 ± 0.067 to 2.571 ± 0.143 BqL-1, with mean of 1.766± 0.399 BqL-1 for 226Ra; 1.736 ± 0.112 to 7.807 ± 0.099 BqL-1, with mean of 3.688 ± 1.371 BqL-1 for 232Th and 149.000 ± 38.480 to 242.900 ± 59.700 BqL-1 with mean of 220.229 ± 22.297 BqL-1 for 40K. The potential radiological health risks evaluated show mean values for Raeq, DAb, AEID and AGED as 23.976 ± 0.446 BqL-1, 12.232 ± 1.445 nGyh-1, 0.060 ± 0.007 mSvy-1 and 0.090 ± 0.027 mSvy-1, respectively. The radiation dose received by age group is in order of infant (≤ 1 year) &gt; teenagers (12-17 years) &gt; children (1-12 years) &gt; adult (&gt; 17 years). The findings reveal that the activity concentration levels and estimated radiological health risks are within permissible limits set by UNSCEAR guidelines. Therefore, consumption of bottled water is radiologically safe. However, findings also suggests that 12 out of 1000 individuals may suffer cancer fatality while 6 out of 1 million individuals may experience hereditary effects over lifetime, from consumption of bottled water. Regular monitoring and stringent regulatory controls are recommended to ensure the radiological safety of natural spring mineral bottled water in South Africa.
